# Material 3 Expressive color rules in Rovia

How color works in this project, and why. Read this before adding or
changing any color.

## The rules

1. **Only scheme roles.** Every fill and every text/icon color in normal
   UI is a `ColorScheme` role: `primary` / `secondary` / `tertiary`
   (plus `*Container` and `on*`), `error` (plus `*Container` and
   `on*`), `surface`, `onSurface`, `onSurfaceVariant`,
   `surfaceContainerLowest` / `Low` / `surfaceContainer` / `High` /
   `Highest`, `surfaceBright` / `surfaceDim`, `outline` /
   `outlineVariant`, `inverseSurface` / `inverseOnSurface` /
   `inversePrimary`, the `*Fixed` roles, `scrim`, `surfaceTint`.
2. **Pairing.** Text and icons always use the `on*` role paired with the
   surface or container they sit on: `onSurface` on any surface or
   `surfaceContainer*`, `onPrimaryContainer` on `primaryContainer`,
   `onSurfaceVariant` for low-emphasis text. A container color is never
   used as text, and an `on*` color is never used as a fill.
3. **Tone-based containers, not elevation.** Hierarchy comes from
   choosing `surfaceContainerLowest` through `surfaceContainerHighest`,
   not from tonal-elevation overlays. Components that set
   `tonalElevation = 0.dp` stay that way.
4. **Dynamic color carries the system theme.** On Android 12+ the scheme
   is generated by the system from the wallpaper and the user's theme
   level. Android 17 QPR2 exposes that level as natural / soft / bright /
   bold. The app must *use* the dynamic scheme (`RoviaTheme` in
   `ui/theme/Theme.kt`) and must not hardcode its own colors anywhere in
   normal UI, or the user's theme-level choice has no effect. The static
   expressive schemes are only the fallback for devices without dynamic
   color. Contrast levels (standard / medium / high) are also
   system-driven; do not re-implement them.
5. **No alpha on flat UI colors.** A static color is never dimmed with
   `.copy(alpha = ...)` in normal UI. Emphasis is expressed by picking a
   different solid role (usually `onSurfaceVariant` for secondary text,
   `surfaceContainerHighest` for a muted fill, `outline` for a dimmed
   disabled icon), or by typography (size / weight). The Material spec's
   own disabled colors are alpha-based; this project deliberately uses
   the solid-role equivalents instead, so the theme level is never
   diluted by a hardcoded opacity.

## What was changed (2026-11-21)

| Area | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Theme.kt` (`RoviaTheme`) | dark fallback `darkColorScheme()` with no comment | Same fallback (see the note below), plus a comment explaining that dynamic color is what carries the Android 17 QPR2 theme levels |
| `WavySeekBar` inactive track | `primaryContainer.copy(alpha = 0.2f)` | `surfaceContainerHighest` |
| `TrackMenu` menu-item disabled text/icons | `onSurface.copy(alpha = 0.38f)` | `onSurfaceVariant` (solid low-emphasis role) |
| `TrackMenu` / `LyricMenu` menu-button disabled icon | `onSurfaceVariant.copy(alpha = 0.38f)` | `outline` — the enabled icon already uses `onSurfaceVariant`, so disabled steps down to the next dimmer in-scheme neutral role |
| `HomeScreen` Wrapped card subtitle | `onPrimaryContainer.copy(alpha = 0.8f)` | solid `onPrimaryContainer`; hierarchy comes from the smaller `bodySmall` type against the bold `titleMedium` |

`MiniPlayer`, `QueueSheet`, and the rest of the UI already used solid
scheme roles and needed no change. `res/values/themes.xml` already uses
the system dynamic neutral colors (`system_neutral2_50` / `_900`) and
was left alone. There is no `colors.xml`, no `surfaceColorAtElevation`
usage, and no other hardcoded seed scheme in the project.

## The artwork exemption (locked 2026-11-21)

**Artwork-backed zones are exempt from the rules above.** Text on
artwork stays white, including its existing white-with-alpha secondary
text, because `ArtworkBackdrop` is a blur, not a background suited for
colorful colors: scheme roles are unreadable on it. White plus alpha is
the hierarchy mechanism there, and it stays exactly as it is — do not
"fix" it to `onSurface` / `onSurfaceVariant`, do not wrap those zones
in a local dark scheme, and do not remove the alpha.

Exempt files (everything that renders on top of `ArtworkBackdrop`, or
on an equivalent blurred palette backdrop):

- `ui/components/ArtworkBackdrop.kt` — the blur backdrop itself,
  including its scrim gradients and the hardcoded
  `fallbackArtworkColor` values (`0xFF17171B` / `0xFFF7F5F8`, used
  only when there is no artwork at all). The HSV artwork-derived
  backdrop color is content-based color, which Material sanctions;
  it was never touched.
- `ui/components/Lyric.kt` — lyric lines, picking highlight, and the
  luminous/reveal canvas effects on the lyric screen.
- `ui/components/LyricShareBottomSheet.kt` — the share card drawn on
  the artwork backdrop.
- `feature/player/PlayerScreen.kt` — title, artist, time labels,
  source line, transport buttons, and the `surfaceContainerHigh`
  button container.
- `feature/player/PlayerLyric.kt` — header and lyric area over the
  backdrop.
- `feature/player/AudioOutput.kt` — the output indicator button
  (`buttonContentColor = Color.White`); it is only ever shown on the
  player screen, on the artwork.
- `feature/artist/ArtistPage.kt` — hero header over the artwork.
- `feature/wrapped/WrappedScreen.kt` — the whole screen sits on the
  artwork backdrop, including the progress segments.
- `feature/playlist/PlaylistScreen.kt` — renders over its own blurred
  palette backdrop (`PlaylistBackdrop`), the same class of background;
  its scrim gradient stays `Color.Black` as it was.
- `feature/album/AlbumPage.kt`, `feature/single/SinglePage.kt`,
  `feature/genre/GenrePage.kt`, `feature/likes/LikedScreen.kt` —
  other `ArtworkBackdrop` callers; they had no alpha or hardcoded
  color issues and were left untouched.

`BackdropContentTheme` (`ui/theme/Theme.kt`) is the pre-existing local
dark scheme already used by `ArtistPage` and `PlaylistScreen`. It was
not extended to any new screen as part of this rework.

**Update 2026-11-21 — content-based color:** the exemption above now
applies to *text on the blur only*. Shaped elements on artwork screens
(buttons, cards, sheets) take their colors from the artwork — see
"Content-based color from artwork" below. Text on the blur still stays
white and is never a scheme role.

## Content-based color from artwork (2026-11-21)

Artwork screens feel more alive when the buttons and other shaped
elements take their colors from the artwork. This is Material 3
content-based dynamic color: the same HCT algorithm dynamic color
uses, seeded from in-app content (the album artwork) instead of the
wallpaper. Text drawn directly on the blurred backdrop still stays
white — a scheme `on*` role is only ever used on a scheme
surface/container, never on the blur.

### How the seed is extracted

`ArtworkBackdrop` already sampled its downscaled artwork bitmap
(144 px max dimension) to compute the backdrop color: a weighted
average hue plus an average saturation, with fallback hue 258.0 and
saturation 0.18 when no colorful pixel qualifies. That sampling is now
a single pass (`sampleArtworkColors`) that yields both the backdrop
color and a seed color — the same hue and measured saturation at a mid
value (0.7), so HCT can derive a full scheme from it. The bitmap is
never scanned twice, and the artwork is never loaded a second time
for color: the seed is reported through the new `onSeedColor`
callback on `ArtworkBackdrop`, from the bitmap the backdrop already
loaded. The fallback seed is the same 258.0 / 0.18 hue and saturation
at value 0.7.

### The scheme

`ui/theme/ArtworkContentTheme.kt` builds the scheme with
`Hct.fromInt(seedArgb)` → `SchemeContent(hct, isDark, 0.0)`
(contrast level 0.0 = standard) and maps every `DynamicScheme` role
into a Compose `ColorScheme` through the full constructor (with
`surfaceContainer*` and the fixed roles). `SchemeContent` is the
canonical variant for content-based color; swapping it for
`SchemeExpressive` or `SchemeVibrant` is a one-line change in
`contentColorScheme` if a more vivid scheme is wanted. Two roles are
kept from the ambient scheme by design, never hardcoded: `scrim` and
`surfaceTint` — the dim behind sheets and dialogs stays consistent
with the surrounding app chrome instead of being re-tinted by the
artwork.

`ArtworkContentTheme(seedColor, darkTheme, content)` provides the
scheme via `MaterialTheme`. The seed is held in a `remember`ed
nullable state per screen and recomputed when the artwork changes;
the scheme itself is built in a `remember` keyed on the seed, the
dark flag, and the ambient scheme. There is no color animation for
now: the scheme swaps when the track or artwork changes. The
`isDark` flag follows the zone — `true` where `BackdropContentTheme`
already forces a dark scheme, `isSystemInDarkTheme()` where the page
follows the app theme.

### Which screens are wrapped

| Screen | Wrapper placement | Seed source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PlayerScreen` | around the non-lyric branch only; `PlayerLyricScreen` is never wrapped | `ArtworkBackdrop.onSeedColor` |
| `ArtistPage`, `AlbumPage`, `SinglePage`, `GenrePage`, `LikedScreen` | inside `BackdropContentTheme`, `darkTheme = true` | `ArtworkBackdrop.onSeedColor` |
| `PlaylistScreen` | inside `BackdropContentTheme`, `darkTheme = true` | the palette container color from `playlistArtworkColors(pageTitle)`, read from the ambient dark scheme outside the content theme so the seed never feeds back into itself |
| `WrappedScreen` | around `WrappedStory` only; the null/empty branches keep the ambient background and are not wrapped | `ArtworkBackdrop.onSeedColor` |
| `LyricShareBottomSheet` | around the `ModalBottomSheet` call, so the sheet container tints too | `onSeedColor` threaded through `LyricShareCard` into its `ArtworkBackdrop` |

`Lyric.kt` and `PlayerLyric.kt` are not touched at all: lyric display
is excluded. `LyricLinePreview` (the lyric preview on the player
screen) keeps its own white `MaterialTheme` override, so it stays
white inside the wrapped player branch.

### What changes color, and what does not

Only elements with a background or shape change: the player playback
controls (they already read `MaterialTheme.colorScheme` into
`playbackColorScheme`, so wrapping tints them automatically), the
Play / shuffle / like `FilledIconButton`s and `Button`s, cards
(`ArtistRecentReleaseCard`, the Wrapped story `Card`), sheets and
menus (`QueueSheet`, `TrackInfoBottomSheet`, `AudioPipelineBottomSheet`,
`TrackMenu`, the share sheet), `WavySeekBar`, and `TrackList` rows
(`secondaryContainer` / `primaryContainer` selections). Everything
else keeps its current colors.

Text on the blur was audited per screen and changed to solid white
where it read a scheme `on*` role:

- `AlbumPage`, `SinglePage`, `GenrePage`, `LikedScreen`: hero title
  → white, hero artist/count → white 70%, empty-state text → white
  70%.
- `ArtistPage`: carousel section title → white; carousel item title
  → white (kept `primary` for the currently playing item — an accent,
  not an `on*` role); carousel supporting text and top-song artist →
  white 70%; top-song title → white (kept `primary` when current).
  The hero name/count were already white. `ArtistRecentReleaseCard`
  text sits on its `surfaceContainerHigh` container and keeps its
  scheme roles, as do the `PlayAndLikeButtonGroup` button contents.
- `PlaylistScreen`: hero and empty-state title → white, track count /
  no-tracks text → white 70%. The big blurred name inside
  `PlaylistBackdrop` keeps its palette content color, which is paired
  with its palette container by construction.
- `WrappedScreen`: overlay title → white, overlay subtitle → white
  70%, close `IconButton` content → white. The progress segments keep
  their `onSurface` / `primary` bars (not text or icons), and the
  slide content inside the story `Card` keeps its scheme roles on the
  `surfaceContainer` card.
- `PlayerScreen`: all on-blur text was already hardcoded white; no
  text change was needed. The `TrackMenu` items read `onSurface` /
  `onSurfaceVariant` over the transparent menu on the blur — the same
  readability as before the wrap in both themes, so they are kept and
  noted here.
- `LyricShareBottomSheet`: the sheet title sits on the sheet container
  and keeps `onSurface`; the share card text was already hardcoded
  white. The exported card renders identically: the card's backdrop
  `isDarkTheme` derives from the content scheme's surface, whose
  dark/light matches the ambient app theme.

### Fallback when there is no artwork

When the seed is null, `ArtworkContentTheme` keeps the ambient scheme
for that screen — on dark-forced pages that is
`BackdropContentTheme`'s dynamic dark scheme, elsewhere the app
scheme — so a screen with no artwork looks exactly as it did before
the content theme existed.

### Build-verify item

The dependency is MDC-Android, `com.google.android.material:material:1.13.0`
(latest stable, September 2025), added to `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and as
`implementation(...)` in `app/build.gradle.kts` (accessor
`libs.google.material`). There is NO standalone
`com.google.android.material:material-color-utilities` artifact on Maven
Central or Google Maven — verified 2026-11-21: the metadata file, the
Central artifact page, and Central search all return 404 / zero results,
and the upstream README lists the Java implementation's location as
MDC-Android only. The `0.4.0` seen in search results belongs to
`org.mvnpm.at.material`, an npm mirror, not Google's artifact. The
`Hct` / `SchemeContent` classes used here ship inside the `material`
artifact itself: `SchemeContent(Hct, Boolean, Double)` was verified in
the MDC master source
(`lib/java/com/google/android/material/color/utilities/SchemeContent.java`).
The same first build must confirm the `ColorScheme` full-constructor
parameter names used in `contentColorScheme` and the Gradle accessor
name. No other dependency was added, and no third-party theming library
is used.

## Top app bars: solid on main pages, transparent on artwork pages (2026-11-21)

Main pages use a **solid** top area in `surface`: Home, Recently Added
and History use a solid `TopAppBar` (`containerColor` and
`scrolledContainerColor` are both `surface`); Library uses a solid
`surface` background behind its custom category header row, and Search
behind its search field. All of them sit below the status bar at the
same height as before (`windowInsets = WindowInsets(0, 0, 0, 0)` plus
`.statusBarsPadding()` on the `TopAppBar`s, background outside the
status-bar padding on the custom headers so the strip is covered too).
The list's top inset (`contentTopPadding`) is **layout** padding on the
`LazyColumn`/`TrackList` modifier, not scrollable content padding, so
items are clipped at the header's bottom edge and never slide through
the header or the status bar. The bottom inset stays scrollable content
padding, so the list keeps flowing under the navigation bar — top
bounded, bottom full-screen, by design.

Library's category tabs are the one exception to clipping: their start
inset lives **inside** the horizontally scrolling row (like the folder
breadcrumb), so at rest the first tab starts at the usual padding, but
scrolling can bring it all the way to the left edge. The right side
stays clipped by the settings button. In the Folders category the
folder breadcrumb is the **second row of the same top bar**, directly
below the tabs with no gap; the folder list starts below the bar +
breadcrumb + spacing.

Artwork pages (Artist, Album, Single, Genre, Liked, Playlist, Wrapped,
Player) keep the transparent bar and the full-screen edge-to-edge
artwork experience: their lists still scroll behind the bar and the
status bar, over the blurred artwork. Settings pages (Settings, Audio,
Folder Filter, About) use the same solid-bar mechanism as the main
pages — explicit `surface` colors, `windowInsets = WindowInsets(0, 0, 0, 0)`
plus `.statusBarsPadding()` — instead of the `TopAppBar` defaults. The
Folder Filter list's `RoundedCornerShape` outer clip is removed (it was
the only list that curved its scrolling content); its items keep their
own segmented rounding.

## Other deliberate exceptions

- **Animation-driven alpha stays.** Opacity that is an animation or
  transition progress is not a color choice: the lyric gap-dot wave
  (`Lyric.kt`, `accentColor.copy(alpha = alpha)` where `alpha` is the
  lit progress) and the luminous bloom mask
  (`Color.White.copy(alpha = growth.bloom)`) keep their alpha.
- **Scrim and fade gradients stay.** A gradient over artwork is an
  image treatment, not a flat color: the top scrims and the vertical
  backdrop washes in `ArtworkBackdrop` / `PlaylistScreen` keep their
  varying alpha. They live in exempt files and were left as-is.
- **DstIn mask values are not colors.** `Color.White`,
  `Color.Black`, and `Color.Transparent` used with `BlendMode.DstIn`
  (lyric fading edges, the soft lyric reveal, the hero artwork edge
  fade) are alpha-mask values — opaque means keep, transparent means
  cut — not UI colors. They stay.
- **`Color.Transparent` as "no fill" stays.** It is the absence of a
  color, not a color role.

## Build-verify item

**`expressiveDarkColorScheme()` does not exist.** The expressive
baseline palette is light-only: `expressiveLightColorScheme()` ships,
but there is no dark counterpart (verified against material3 1.5.0
alpha 26; the Compose BOM here is 2026.10.01). The dark fallback
therefore stays the baseline `darkColorScheme()`, as the code comment
in `Theme.kt` says. If a future material3 release adds an expressive
dark scheme, the change is one line in `RoviaTheme`.
